- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.10) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots downward — cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at 80–82 unless sentiment turns positive.
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.30 in 3–5 days), model underreacts — increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days to align with sentiment trend.
- Model consistently underestimates downward moves after 7–10 days of high prices — apply 3–5% downward bias to forecast if recent 10-day average is >80 and sentiment is negative.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly negative but price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — add 1–3% upward bias to forecast for next 5–7 days to counteract overcorrection.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns negative within 3 days, adjust forecast 3–5 days ahead by -2–4% to reflect sentiment decay.
